title: The meta-frameworks: Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit and Angular SSR — routing, server rendering and static generation

videos.script:
Lesson 1 built server rendering by hand, in one small file. This lesson looks at the four products that do it for a living. {{four}} Next.js for React. Nuxt for Vue. SvelteKit for Svelte. And Angular's own server rendering. You took one of those frameworks. You do not need the other three to follow along.

{{same}} Each one builds the same two pages of the planner. The list of courses, and one course. Same data, same addresses. {{files}} You will see how a folder becomes an address, or a list does, and where the data is read.

{{build}} Then you build all four and run them side by side. They all send the finished page. {{weigh}} What differs is everything that comes with it. You will weigh the JavaScript each page runs, and look inside the page at the data it carries.

{{refuse}} Two of them will surprise you on the way. One refuses to render for a host it does not know. One answers a missing page with a 200.

{{choose}} And at the end, the question that matters more than which one. Whether this app needs one at all.
